questions.question: Explain how you would obtain salt crystals from salt water, and why this method loses the water.
questions.expected_answer: Pour the salt water into an evaporating dish and heat it gently (or leave it in the Sun) so the water evaporates; when most water has gone, crystals of salt form; heat gently at the end and wear goggles because it can spit. The water turns into vapour and escapes into the air, so it is not collected; only the solid solute remains. Slow evaporation (crystallisation) gives larger, purer crystals.

questions.question: Describe simple distillation of salt water, naming the apparatus and explaining what happens at each stage, and give two uses of distillation.
questions.expected_answer: Salt water is heated in a flask (with boiling chips); the water boils at 100 degrees Celsius and turns to vapour, leaving the salt behind; the vapour passes into a condenser, a tube cooled by cold running water, where it condenses into liquid; the pure water (distillate) is collected in a beaker; a thermometer shows the vapour temperature. Uses: making distilled water for batteries and laboratories; desalination of seawater; separating crude oil into fractions such as petrol and diesel (fractional distillation); extracting essential oils from plants such as buchu.

questions.question: Describe how paper chromatography can show that a black ink is a mixture, and explain why the start line is drawn in pencil and the spot kept above the solvent.
questions.expected_answer: Draw a pencil line about 2 cm from the bottom of chromatography paper and place a small spot of ink on it; stand the paper in a little solvent (water) with the spot above the solvent level. The solvent soaks up the paper, dissolves the dyes and carries them upward; each dye travels a different distance depending on how well it dissolves and how strongly it clings to the paper, so the black ink separates into several coloured spots, showing it is a mixture. Pencil is used because graphite does not dissolve and run; the spot is above the solvent so that the ink is carried up the paper instead of dissolving into the solvent in the container.
